title: ANCHOR INVESTMENTS AND TEXTILE VALUE-CHAIN
body_text:
PM MITRA Parks are a government initiative with scheme outlay of Rs. 4,445 Crore for the period 2021-22 to 2027-28 to create world-class, integrated textile manufacturing hubs across seven states in India to boost investment, employment, and exports. These parks are inspired by the ‘5F’ vision (Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign) and aim to develop a complete textile value chain, from spinning to garmenting, with modern infrastructure and facilities. The seven selected locations are in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra.
The PM MITRA Park scheme provides for the development of core infrastructure, including developed factory sites, plug-and-play facilities, incubation centres, roads, power, water and wastewater systems, as well as support infrastructure, including CETPs, workers’ hostels & housing, logistics parks, warehousing, medical facilities, and training & skill development facilities. Further, up to 10% of the park area may be utilized for commercial development, including shops & offices, shopping malls, hotels and convention centers.
At present, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed with all States and 100% land has been acquired for all the sites. Environmental Clearances have been received for all PM MITRA Parks. Joint Venture Agreements have been signed and SPVs incorporated for all 5 greenfield sites. DPRs amounting to ₹13,537 crore have been finalized for all 7 States. Investment interests amounting to ₹68,590 crore have been received so far by the PM MITRA States. External infrastructure works amounting to ₹2,736 crore are under development, against which ₹797.30 crore has been expended so far. Internal infrastructure works for development of core infrastructure amounting to ₹1,720 crore have commenced across all States, against which ₹524 crore has been expended so far.
The Ministry received 18 proposals from 13 states for setting up Parks under the scheme. 7 sites were selected out of which 5 are under the Greenfield category and 2 fall under the brownfield category. In Budget 2026-27, the new scheme for establishment of Mega Textile Parks is announced. The Government will request all State Governments to submit proposals in due course.
This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.
*****
MAM/VN
(Lok Sabha US Q3721)

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Textiles informed Lok Sabha that under the PM MITRA Parks scheme (outlay Rs. 4,445 crore, 2021-22 to 2027-28), all 7 selected sites across Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra have completed MoUs, 100% land acquisition, and environmental clearances. DPRs worth Rs. 13,537 crore have been finalized, and investment interest of Rs. 68,590 crore has been received, with external and internal infrastructure works underway. The Budget 2026-27 also announced a new Mega Textile Parks scheme, for which states will be asked to submit proposals.
enrichment.context:
PM MITRA (Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) Parks were approved in 2021 to create integrated textile value chains within single locations, reducing logistics costs and fragmentation that have historically hurt Indian textile competitiveness against countries like Bangladesh and Vietnam. The '5F' vision (Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign) reflects the government's push to integrate raw material production with manufacturing and exports, aligning with the broader 'Make in India' and PLI (Production Linked Incentive) initiatives for textiles. The scheme uses a hub-and-spoke model with a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) structure involving both central and state governments, similar to industrial corridor projects.

The textile sector is significant for India's economy as the second-largest employer after agriculture and a major foreign exchange earner. Delays in land acquisition and infrastructure in earlier industrial park schemes (like SITPs) have often hampered investment; hence the emphasis here on 100% land acquisition and environmental clearances signals progress. The announcement of a new Mega Textile Parks scheme in Budget 2026-27 suggests the government intends to scale up this integrated-park model further, potentially addressing gaps or expanding capacity beyond the original seven PM MITRA sites.

prelims_questions.question: The PM MITRA Parks scheme is associated with which of the following visions?
options: 5F: Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that PM MITRA Parks are inspired by the '5F' vision: Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign, aimed at developing a complete textile value chain.

prelims_questions.question: How many states have been selected for setting up PM MITRA Parks, and how many of these sites are greenfield?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that 7 sites were selected from 18 proposals by 13 states, with 5 falling under greenfield and 2 under brownfield categories.
